\chapter{Shop, Item, and Price: One New Vowel Mark}
\label{ch:mw-shopping-three}
\hlchaptermodality{18}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can recognise, say, read, and write shop, item, and price after learning only the short-u vowel mark.}

Three source-attested shopping words begin by ear, add one vowel mark, and finish in four separately scored skills without claiming a complete buying exchange.
\end{chapteropening}

\section[dukān]{Hear \emph{dukān} — shop}

\label{lesson:MW-C13-hear-dukan}



\begin{quote}
Recall the six-word weather payoff, say market, then write \textbf{\mw{मौसम}}, \textbf{\mw{गर्मी}}, and \textbf{\mw{ठंडी}}, then form \textbf{\mw{ि}} once.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{dukān} — \textbf{shop}
\end{quote}

Hear the two beats and say the word once from a shop cue. Keep the sound and meaning together; the unfamiliar vowel mark waits for the next lesson.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[u]{\mw{ु} — short \emph{u} after a consonant}

\label{lesson:MW-W13-u-matra}



\begin{quote}
Say shop, write \textbf{\mw{द}}, \textbf{\mw{ू}}, \textbf{\mw{ौ}}, \textbf{\mw{ड}}, \textbf{\mw{ल}}, and \textbf{\mw{पत्नी}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Script — one mark}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{ु}} — short \emph{u} after a consonant
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Trace \textbf{\mw{ु}} below \textbf{\mw{द}} once, copy \textbf{\mw{दु}} once, cover it, and write \textbf{\mw{दु}} from sound. Keep it shorter than familiar \textbf{\mw{दू}}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.unicode.org/charts/PDF/U0900.pdf}{Unicode Devanagari chart}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[dukān]{\mw{दुकान} — shop on the page}

\label{lesson:MW-C13-dukan}



\begin{quote}
Say shop and market, write \textbf{\mw{बाजार}}, \textbf{\mw{बरसात}}, and \textbf{\mw{कांई}}, then write \textbf{\mw{पाछे} \mw{मिलसू}}, then form \textbf{\mw{दु}}, \textbf{\mw{का}}, and \textbf{\mw{न}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{दु}} + \textbf{\mw{कान}} $\to$ \textbf{\mw{दुकान}} — \emph{dukān} — shop
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Look, cover, wait five seconds, and write \textbf{\mw{दुकान}}. Check short \textbf{\mw{ु}} below the first sign and long \textbf{\mw{ा}} in the second chunk.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[vastu]{Hear \emph{vastu} — item}

\label{lesson:MW-C13-hear-vastu}



\begin{quote}
Say and write shop, form short \textbf{\mw{ु}}, then recall money, temple, and cold, then retrieve the see-you-later line from its cue.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{vastu} — \textbf{item; thing}
\end{quote}

Say the two beats once from an item cue. The word can name the thing being bought; no buying sentence is claimed yet.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[vastu]{\mw{वस्तु} — item on the page}

\label{lesson:MW-C13-vastu}



\begin{quote}
Say item and shop, write \textbf{\mw{दुकान}}, \textbf{\mw{गर्मी}}, and \textbf{\mw{हाथ}}, then say mother, then form short \textbf{\mw{ु}} and the familiar vowel-off mark \textbf{\mw{्}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{वस्}} + \textbf{\mw{तु}} $\to$ \textbf{\mw{वस्तु}} — \emph{vastu} — item
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Look, cover, wait five seconds, and write \textbf{\mw{वस्तु}}. Check the middle consonant join and the final short \textbf{\mw{ु}}.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[bhāv]{Hear \emph{bhāv} — price}

\label{lesson:MW-C13-hear-bhaav}



\begin{quote}
Say and write item and shop, then recall market and write money and cloud, then write \textbf{\mw{मां}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\emph{bhāv} — \textbf{price}
\end{quote}

Say the single long beat from a price-tag cue. This lesson teaches the noun; asking the final price remains later phrase work.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[bhāv]{\mw{भाव} — price on the page}

\label{lesson:MW-C13-bhaav}



\begin{quote}
Say price, item, shop, and father. Write \textbf{\mw{वस्तु}}, \textbf{\mw{बाप}}, and \textbf{\mw{हवा}}, then form familiar \textbf{\mw{भ}}, \textbf{\mw{ा}}, and \textbf{\mw{व}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{What to know first}
\begin{quote}
\textbf{\mw{भा}} + \textbf{\mw{व}} $\to$ \textbf{\mw{भाव}} — \emph{bhāv} — price
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Look, cover, wait five seconds, and write \textbf{\mw{भाव}}. Hold the long vowel in speech and keep \textbf{\mw{ा}} after \textbf{\mw{भ}} in writing.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Retrieve shop, item, and price}

\label{lesson:MW-R13-shopping-three}



\begin{quote}
Write \textbf{\mw{ु}}, \textbf{\mw{ौ}}, \textbf{\mw{ग}}, \textbf{\mw{ड}}, and \textbf{\mw{ब}}, then recall the six-word weather payoff.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Hear the three words in mixed order, say each from its meaning, match three printed cards, then write all three from sound.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Payoff — three shopping words in four skills}

\label{lesson:MW-C13-shopping-three}



\begin{quote}
Say market, write money, recall the weather payoff, then ask and answer the known wellbeing exchange, then write \textbf{\mw{बाप}}.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
1. Identify three heard words. 2. Produce three words from meaning cues. 3. Match three printed cards to meanings. 4. Write all three heard words without a model.

Pass each skill separately.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Source: \href{https://www.marwaripathshala.com/marwari-lesson-9-english}{Marwari Pathshala, Lesson 9}.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[Practice]{Close the first shopping loop}

\label{lesson:MW-R13-shopping-close}



\begin{quote}
Write \textbf{\mw{ु}}, \textbf{\mw{घ}}, \textbf{\mw{ज}}, and \textbf{\mw{त}}; say brother; retrieve cloud, rain, weather, heat, and cold; write \textbf{\mw{ड}}, \textbf{\mw{गर्मी}}, and \textbf{\mw{ठंडी}}; then recall the three-word weather payoff and name the four shopping-payoff skills.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Without a model, hear one word, say its meaning, read the other two in mixed order, then write all three from meaning cues.

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]

\end{tcolorbox}
